subject: Hosted API latency coverage & measurement window proposal — BrightBridge
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: ops@brightbridge.com, contracts@brightbridge.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0000
Subject: Hosted API latency coverage & measurement window proposal — BrightBridge

Hi Ben / BrightBridge team,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. To keep momentum on the SLA conversation, attaching a concise proposal for how Redwood would measure and commit to latency SLOs for your hosted API usage. High-level asks: please confirm which models and traffic patterns you expect to run in production (short-chat vs long-infer), and whether regional enforcement by us-east only is acceptable.

Summary of what we're proposing (attached as CSV for easy redlines):
- Two commitment tiers: Standard (no credits) and Enterprise (SLA-backed credits)
- Measurement unit: request-level tail latency (end-to-end HTTP response time measured at ingress)
- Percentiles reported: p50 and p95
- Measurement windows: rolling 24-hour window for reporting; contractual look-back for crediting is rolling 30-day window.
- Aggregation: per-region, per-model family (small/medium/large), with weighted percentiles by request count

Proposed numeric targets for Enterprise tier (examples in attachment):
- p50: <= 60 ms (short-chat workloads)
- p95: <= 350 ms (short-chat workloads)
- For larger context or >2048-token inputs, we include an exception policy (see section below).

Exception policy (what triggers an SLA exemption):
- Planned maintenance windows (>=30 minutes) with 72-hour advance notice
- Customer traffic patterns that exceed an agreed token-length profile (e.g., consistent >4096-token requests) — these are excluded from p95 calculation unless specifically rolled into the committed profile
- Model variants not in Redwood's verified catalog (we'll list supported models in the final contract)

Next steps: please review the attached CSV and the short diagram; if the measurement windows look good, we'll draft contract language and put it into DocuSign for signature. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk the math.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Jordan — thanks for the note and the quick turnaround. A couple quick clarifying questions before we escalate to procurement: 

1) When you say 'rolling 24-hour window' for reporting vs 'rolling 30-day window' for crediting, can you define how p95 is computed (sampled every minute from the ingress vs t-digest on full set)? Procurement will want deterministic wording.

2) The numeric targets look reasonable for short-chat, but BrightBridge runs a mix of low-latency widgets (<= 200 tokens) and some nightly batch enrichments (~10k tokens). Can you confirm batch-style requests are excluded or treated under a different profile?

3) What is the proposed SLA credit formula if p95 exceeds the target in a 30-day window?

If you can send a short paragraph per item (and a link to the contract language), we can route to our procurement team this week.

Subject: Re: Hosted API latency coverage & measurement window proposal — BrightBridge

Ben — great questions, thanks. Short answers below and I'm attaching a one-paragraph redline you can pass to procurement.

1) p95 computation method — proposal
- Production: we compute request-level latencies at ingress (time request received by our front-door to the last byte sent) and aggregate using a t-digest approach sampled at 1-minute intervals to keep memory bounded. The effective p95 is computed from the aggregated t-digests across the rolling window (24hr for dashboarding, 30-day for credits).
- Rationale: t-digest preserves extreme tail behavior properly when you have millions of small/large requests and keeps deterministic recomputation possible for audit.

2) Batch / long-context handling
- Batch jobs and long-token jobs: we will classify requests that exceed an agreed token-length threshold (default 2048 tokens unless you ask for 4096) as 'long-context' and measure them under a separate profile. Long-context requests will not be counted toward the short-chat p95 target unless BrightBridge explicitly opts them into the same profile. This avoids penalizing us for distinct workload classes.

3) Credit formula (proposed)
- If Enterprise p95 target is missed in the contractual 30-day window, credits are calculated as a percent of that month's invoice: 5% credit for a single 30-day window breach, 10% if breach occurs in two consecutive 30-day windows, capped at 25% per month. Credits are only payable when breach is outside of exclusion criteria (maintenance, agreed-exception loads).

Attached: exception-clause-draft.docx (one-paragraph redline you can paste into procurement). If this looks good, we'll generate final contract language and a DocuSign packet.

I'll mark a couple of optional tweaks for Marissa and Karthik below.

—Jordan
